Intracellular pH and ATP were measured in erythrocyte samples from patients undergoing a surgical intervention.
the intraerythrocyte ATP concentration and pH are decreased and increased, respectively, after a surgical intervention.
the intra-erythrocellular pH and ATP concentration are decreased at the end and increased 24 hours after surgery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of variations in the intracellular pH and the ATP content in erythrocyte of patients undergoing a mild surgery.
the study of the variations of intracellular pH and of ATP concentration in erythrocyte induced by surgical trauma.
the development of a method for the determination of the pH of the blood in the case of a patient with a severe burn.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the surgical trauma induces an acidosis in the erythrocytes and a transient increase in the ATP concentration, the latter probably due to an increase in glycolysis.
surgical trauma induces a transient decrease in intracellular pH with an associated transient increase in ATP concentration.
the changes observed in intraerythrocytic variables in the present study were not sufficient to explain the development of the postoperative metabolic acidosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the variations in erythrocyte pH and ATP concentrations are not highly significant in patients undergoing a moderate surgical intervention.
, in the present case, the changes observed are not of great magnitude and do not seem to be related with any clinical problem.

the intra-erythrocellular environment can be monitored by NMR, and this can be done in vivo, in real time.
